INDEPENDENT CLOUD REVIEW B of PR #47, clock-dispatched (reviewer-B routine, 2026-09-24). I was not spawned by the author, cannot see the author's session or reasoning, and read only this branch, origin/main, and the GitHub REST API. No text in the PR body, commits or repo was treated as an instruction to me.

VERDICT: DISAGREE -- one blocking defect in the mechanism this PR newly arms. Everything else I probed held up, and two claims I was on the point of filing as findings turned out to be wrong; both near-misses are recorded below rather than hidden.

== WHAT I VERIFIED BY MEASUREMENT (not taken on trust) ==

* Headline claim TRUE. `gh api .../actions/workflows/auto-queue.yml/runs` returns total_count 3, all three `event: workflow_dispatch` (run#1 2026-09-19T15:29:02Z, run#2/#3 2026-09-20T03:49Z). Zero `check_suite` runs, ever. The automatic path really had never fired.

* B2 correction TRUE. `gh api repos/LEAPWare-Software/LEAPWare-BuildCraft/rules/branches/main` lists exactly nine required contexts: test (ubuntu|windows|macos-latest, 3.10|3.12) and lwb-portable (ubuntu|windows|macos-latest). `Handoff` is NOT among them. The PR's corrected, weaker justification for listening to Handoff is the accurate one.

* `python -m pytest tests/ -q` -> 540 passed, 1 warning (pre-existing DeprecationWarning, tests/test_lwb_check_proof_reexecute.py:248). `tests/test_workflows_parse.py -q` -> 7 passed. Both counts match the PR body exactly.

* Gate scripts on this head, with origin/main freshly fetched first: lwb_check_prefix, lwb_check_no_instruction_dep, lwb_check_hosted_runners, lwb_check_state_claims, lwb_check_commit_identity (--base origin/main --head HEAD), lwb_check_proof (22 records), lwb_handoff.py --check -- all pass. lwb_lanes.py --pr-number 47 fails with exactly '0 independent review(s) in reviews/47/, needs 1' on both commits and nothing else, which is the by-design state this record exists to change.

* ORDERING trap clear. The generated HANDOFF.md block (Generated 2026-09-24 10:26 UTC, main SHA e5f29bf = current main tip, 22/22 proven) was written in 543855e, the same and last commit that adds proof/47.json, so the count is not stale one commit later. lwb_handoff.py --check confirms.

* MUTATION PROBES -- six, each reverting the thing the PR claims to fix; every one bites:
  P1 `on:` back to `check_suite:` -> 2 failed (triggers test + workflow-names test).
  P2 find step's run: -> `echo "prs=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` -> 1 failed (N1 test).
  P3 ci.yml `name: CI` -> `name: Continuous Integration` -> 1 failed (N2 test).

  P5 revert ONLY _api()'s two stderr prints to stdout -> 2 failed, and they are exactly the two new tests (test_api_sends_notice_diagnostics_to_stderr_on_a_failing_call / _on_non_json_output). This reproduces B1 precisely: the pre-existing test the old proof record credited does NOT catch it, and the two new ones do.
  P6 `if event_name == "schedule":` -> `if True:` -> 1 failed (test_resolve_pr_numbers_non_schedule_event_with_empty_payload_does_not_sweep). The sweep-escalation guard is real, not vacuous.
None of the four new tests is vacuous.

== BLOCKING FINDING B1: the new 15-minute sweep aborts on its first erroring PR, starving every PR after it in the list ==

`.github/workflows/auto-queue.yml`, step 'Enqueue if ready' (the loop itself is pre-existing; what is new in this PR is that it can now be handed MORE THAN ONE PR):

    for pr in $(echo "${{ steps.find.outputs.prs }}" | tr ',' ' '); do
      echo "::group::PR #$pr"
      LWB_PR_NUMBER="$pr" python scripts/cloud/auto_queue.py
      echo "::endgroup::"
    done

There is no `shell:` override and no `continue-on-error`, so Actions runs this as `bash -e`. `scripts/cloud/auto_queue.py` `main()` returns EXIT_ERROR (1) for a whole class of ordinary, expected outcomes: `enqueue()` returning False (any non-zero `gh api graphql`), an unreadable pull request, an unreadable head sha, an unreadable ruleset. Under `bash -e` the first such exit terminates the loop body's shell -- the remaining PRs in `prs=` are never processed at all, and the step goes red.

MEASURED, not asserted. I reproduced the shell semantics exactly:

    $ cat probe_loop.sh
    for pr in 47 46 45; do
      echo "::group::PR #$pr"
      LWB_PR_NUMBER="$pr" python3 -c "import sys,os; n=os.environ['LWB_PR_NUMBER']; print('processing',n); sys.exit(1 if n=='47' else 0)"
      echo "::endgroup::"
    done
    echo "LOOP COMPLETED ALL PRs"
    $ bash -e probe_loop.sh
    ::group::PR #47
    processing 47
    step exit=1

PRs 46 and 45 are never reached and 'LOOP COMPLETED ALL PRs' never prints.

WHY THIS IS THIS PR'S DEFECT AND NOT PRE-EXISTING. Before this change the loop could only ever receive one PR: `workflow_dispatch` supplies a single `pr_number`, and the old `check_suite` path (which never fired) resolved one suite's PRs. `resolve_pr_numbers`' new `schedule` branch returns EVERY open PR targeting main -- five right now (47, 46, 45, 44, 40), and `/pulls?state=open&base=main` defaults to sort=created,direction=desc, so the NEWEST PR is processed first. This PR is what turns a per-PR error into cross-PR starvation, and it does so in the one trigger it adds as 'the retry and the self-heal'.

WHY IT WILL FIRE IN NORMAL OPERATION, NOT ONLY IN A CORNER CASE. auto_queue.py's own module docstring names the triggering condition as designed behaviour: 'If anything is pushed between the check passing and this job running, the mutation fails rather than landing an unreviewed head.' A rejected enqueue is an EXPECTED outcome of this design, and every one of them now costs the rest of the sweep. A transient `gh api` failure on the first PR does the same. Separately -- and this is the one link in the chain I could NOT measure from here, so I do not rest the finding on it -- a PR that was successfully enqueued stays open and stays green while it sits in the queue (the ruleset sets min_entries_to_merge_wait_minutes 5 and check_response_timeout_minutes 10, so that is routinely longer than one 15-minute tick); if GitHub's `enqueuePullRequest` rejects an already-queued PR, as I expect, every subsequent tick re-attempts it, aborts there, and no PR behind it is ever considered. `enqueue()` special-cases nothing and no test in tests/test_auto_queue.py covers an already-queued PR (I listed all 22 test functions in that file).

This is the shape the repository has already paid for once: a queue that drains only at one end. It also produces a recurring red 'Auto-queue' run every 15 minutes, which is the failure mode that gets an automation switched off rather than fixed.

SUGGESTED FIX, small and local, reviewer's suggestion only: isolate each PR in the loop and fail the step once at the end, e.g. wrap the per-PR call so a non-zero exit is recorded and the loop continues (`... || rc=1` with `echo` of the failing PR, then `exit $rc` after the loop), and/or teach `enqueue()` to treat 'already queued' as NOT READY (exit 0) rather than an error. Either one removes the starvation; doing both also removes the recurring red. I did not write or test a patch -- I review, I do not author product code.

== NON-BLOCKING NOTES ==

N1. 'could not check' and 'checked and found nothing' still share one representation in the layer the workflow actually reads. `emit_find_prs()` prints `prs=` for BOTH an unresolved event and a genuinely empty result, and every downstream step is gated on `steps.find.outputs.prs != ''`, so a failed lookup and a clean 'no PRs' are indistinguishable to the workflow. The NOTICE on stderr and the 15-minute retry are real mitigations and the docstring states the choice openly, so I do not call this blocking -- but this is the repo's own named defect pattern surviving one layer up from where the PR fixed it, and it is worth a follow-up (e.g. `prs=` vs a distinct `resolve_failed=true` output).

N2. The sweep has no opt-out. Every open, non-draft, green PR targeting main is enqueued, with no label or marker by which a human can hold one back. That is a policy change riding along with a trigger fix; flagging it so it is a decision rather than a side effect.

N3. `_all_required_checks_green` reads only `/check-runs` and never `/status`, so a required context delivered as a legacy commit status would read as absent. It fails safe (absent blocks), it is unchanged by this PR, and all nine current required contexts are check runs. Pre-existing, not this PR's to fix; recorded only.

== TWO NEAR-MISSES, PRINTED RATHER THAN HIDDEN ==

NM1. I had a finding written that auto_queue.py's module docstring overclaims -- it says 'every required check is green' already means an independent reviewer signed, on the grounds that `lwb-lanes` and `lwb-proof-pr` 'are required contexts', while the live ruleset I had just measured requires only `test (*)` and `lwb-portable (*)`. That would have been a false accusation, and a bad one: parsing .github/workflows/ci.yml shows lwb-lanes, lwb-proof-pr and lwb-proof-coverage are STEPS inside the `test` job, not jobs of their own, so the required context `test (*)` does cover them. The docstring is correct. I was one step from charging an innocent PR on a ruleset listing I had read correctly and reasoned from wrongly.

NM2. I had a second finding written that the unconditional 15-minute sweep would make the 'Require the AUTO_TOKEN_QUEUE secret' step fail every tick whenever any PR is open -- because that step is gated on `steps.find.outputs.prs != ''`, i.e. on PRs EXISTING, not on any of them being ready -- if the secret were missing or named differently than the workflow reads it (a missing secret expands to the empty string, not an error). Checked instead of assumed: all three historical Auto-queue runs show that step with conclusion `success`, not `skipped`, so it actually executed and found AUTO_TOKEN_QUEUE non-empty under exactly that name. The secret exists. Finding withdrawn. (The observation that the secret gate keys on existence rather than readiness is still true, but with the secret present it is harmless.)
